01.text: an open-source, self-hosted AI assistant for German Kitas and childcare providers.

02.text: Kita teams spend hours on paperwork:
letters, minutes, checklists, and the same questions again and again.
Every hour at the desk is an hour away from the children.

03.text: OpenKita AI is not another Kita management system.
It is an assistant that eases existing administration, designed to integrate with open-source Kita software such as KitaLux.

04.text: A Parent Communication Assistant drafts newsletters and invitations in German and English, with experimental Turkish and Arabic that need native review.
An Administration Assistant turns notes into minutes and checklists.
A Knowledge Assistant answers from your documents, with sources.

05.text: Here is a mock-up of the planned flow, with fictional data.
The manager asks for a friendly summer party announcement, with a request for buffet contributions.
The assistant drafts a warm German text, ready to edit.

06.text: Then English, Turkish and Arabic versions appear.
the default local model does not officially support them, so native review is required.
Every draft is marked as AI-generated, and nothing is sent until a person approves it.

07.text: Version 0.1 is designed to be local-only:
external AI is disabled and fails closed, there are no child profiles, and a person approves anything before it is sent.
audit logs, and a Privacy Gateway that detects, minimises and verifies data before anything reaches an optional external provider, only after privacy tests.
This reduces risk; it does not guarantee GDPR compliance.

08.text: Everything is open source, licensed under Apache 2.0:
code, prompts, workflows, schema, API and Docker Compose deployment.
Built with Next.js, FastAPI, PostgreSQL and Ollama.
Model weights have their own licences.

09.text: installation, configuration, integration, training, support and migration.
A test installation for one to three thousand euros is a hypothesis to validate.

10.text: One idea is the OpenKita Box, a private AI appliance installed on premises.
Prices are illustrative hypotheses, hardware obligations still need investigation, and we would sell to providers first.

11.text: the foundation is built, and the AI features are in development.
First we will interview five Kita managers, two providers and two educators, and ask what builds trust.

12.text: version 0.1 is in progress, then the Knowledge Assistant, production readiness with the planned Privacy Gateway, integrations, and a multi-facility 1.0 release.

13.text: Kita managers and Träger, join a thirty-minute interview to help us validate OpenKita AI.
The code is on GitHub; the link and a QR code are on screen.
